questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to go on Erasmus exchange in Europe, and from there my choices were a bit random. I ended up choosing Prague for several reasons. Firstly, I liked the size of the city. Secondly, Charles University offered a large range of interesting courses. Lastly, I was interested in going to Eastern Europe, as I haven't been there much and their history is fascinating. The cost of living is also quite cheap, coming from Copenhagen, and that also played a role.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Going on exchange was one of the best things I've done.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival it was quite easy, and the office at Faculty of Arts at Charles University are very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing out of the normal emails from the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There are a lot of Facebook groups for renting rooms in Prague.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's great. Try not to go with the apartments specifically for erasmus students as they are quite expensive and you can find rooms that are a lot cheaper.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They open up for course registration at a specific time, and then it's first come first served principle because there are a limited amount of space on each course - some bigger than others. But apart from that it's very easy to do, and you have a lot of time to change your courses around (I think it was almost a month).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The office at your host faculty. The other exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly succesful. Some courses didn't provide a description for the course and then i couldn't get them pre-approved by my home university, and the teachers weren't great at answering emails. So I couldn't choose that course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a list of the courses you would like to choose and make it longer than just the required amount of ects points so you're ready for the course registration. Rather register for too many courses in the beginning, as you have time in the following weeks to remove them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Quite easy compared to what I'm used to. The courses are also smaller so they take up less of your time, but then you have more of them.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. The "relationship" between teacher and students are kind of the same - they are not very authoritative or formal.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: My apartment was an apartment for erasmus students, and compared to my friends here who rented rooms in other apartments mine was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of different events for exchange students, and I guess they're a good way to meet people, but for the most part they weren't really my vibe. It was giving Gothersgade.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the first two weeks or so there are a whole calendar of events for exchange students like city walks, pub quiz, day trips, different parties. I didn't really go to them but I think a lot of people did.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of stuff to do in Prague! Museums, theater, cinema, events around the city. And it's quite cheap for students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the Czech countryside for a weekend it's very beautiful! Prague is also an easy city to do weekend trips from - it's close to Germany, Austria, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and so on.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people you meet when you go out. But mostly the local students don't really interact super much with exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The cultural difference is not that big.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very friendly and easy-going people. Very beautiful city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Say yes to almost everything in the beginning, it's how you meet everyone. Walk around and get to know the city. Spend some time researching Facebook events happening. Download RA Guide. Download Pid and get the three month pass - there's a lot of public transport in the city and it's very easy to just jump on and off whenever when you have the pass.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Explore the areas outside of Prague 1 - Holesovice, Vinohrady, Zizkov, Karlin. They are a lot less touristy. Don't pay too much in rent (like I did).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made! I was lucky to find a really great group of people very early in my stay, and I've become very close with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It wasn't really that challenging. Maybe being away from your family and friends at home for a longer period of time, but then again 5 months aren't that long, and you're usually too busy with everything happening to think about it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
